## Quick choux rings or puffs

One choux pastry for both věnečky and větrníčky: extra butter and a 250 °C start. About 80 pieces on two trays.

Rate this recipe

/ 5 ·

### Ingredients

- 250 ml water
- a pinch of salt
- 90 g butter
- 140 g coarse flour (hrubá mouka)
- 4 eggs
- fat, for greasing the trays

### Method

- Bring the water, salt and butter to a boil.
- Reduce the heat and stir in the flour all at once; mix until the dough pulls cleanly away from the pan and is no longer sticky.
- Take it off the heat and let it cool slightly.
- Preheat the oven to 250 °C.
- Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing continuously, until the batter is smooth and slightly elastic.
- Pipe onto the greased trays: two stacked rings for věnečky, or small round mounds for větrníčky.
- Bake at 250 °C for 5 minutes, then reduce to 200 °C and bake for about 5 more minutes. Finish for the last 5 minutes or so at a medium heat until golden. Do not open the oven door while baking.
- Slice them straight away while still hot (this stops the shells tearing later). Cool completely before filling.

The filling is up to you: sweetened whipped cream is the simplest. For věnečky use the vanilla buttercream and rum glaze from the věnečky recipe; for větrníčky use the vanilla pudding cream, caramel whipped cream and caramel glaze from the caramel větrník recipe.

This dough uses a higher butter-to-flour ratio (90 g : 140 g) and a hot 250 °C start, which is why it puffs faster and more reliably.

### Frequently asked questions

*summary:* Why start the choux at 250 °C?

A hot start at 250 °C and a higher butter ratio (90 g to 140 g flour) make the choux rise fast. After 5 minutes drop to 200 °C. About 80 pieces on two trays.

*summary:* Can one dough make both rings and puffs?

Yes. The same choux: pipe rings as two stacked circles and puffs as small mounds. Fill with whipped cream, vanilla cream or caramel as you like.
